clauses: Components and starting health/card setup
Younger and older player placement order, spaces, multizone sidekick rule, Alice size timing
First turn
answers.answer: Use the chosen hero’s matching components. Each player shuffles 30 cards into a separate face-down deck and draws 5; set hero and sidekick health to the reference values (undialed sidekicks 1). Younger places hero at space 1, then sidekicks in separate spaces sharing a zone with that hero; a multizone hero space allows any of those zones. Alice’s controller chooses BIG or SMALL while placing her. Older then places hero at space 2 and sidekicks under the same rules. Younger takes first turn.

evidence.text: 3. Each player shuffles their **30 action cards into one separate face-down deck**, then draws **5 cards**.
2. Set the hero’s and sidekick’s dials to the starting health above; undialed sidekicks have 1 health each.

4. The **younger player** places their hero on starting space **1**, then their sidekick(s) in **separate spaces sharing a zone with that hero**. If the hero’s space belongs to several zones, use any of those zones. Make beginning-of-game decisions when placing that player’s fighters. **Alice’s controller**, whether younger or older, chooses **BIG or SMALL when placing Alice** and displays her size token.
5. The **older player** places their hero on starting space **2**, then places sidekicks under the same rules.
6. The younger player takes the first turn.

clauses: Two actions from the allowed types; repetition and skipping
Hand limit enforcement timing and result with 9 cards
answers.answer: Take 2 actions from maneuver, scheme, and attack; you may repeat an action and cannot skip one. You may hold 9 during your turn, then at turn end discard 2 to your own discard pile, leaving 7 before the opponent’s turn.

evidence.text: At the start of Medusa’s turn, her optional special ability may resolve (see below). Then take **2 actions** from **maneuver, scheme, attack**. You may repeat an action, including maneuver twice; **you cannot skip an action**.
You may hold more than 7 cards during your turn. **At the end of your turn**, discard excess cards to your own discard pile until you have **7**, then the opponent takes their turn.

clauses: Maneuver draw before movement
Each fighter’s movement allowance and independent sequencing
Friendly/enemy pass-through and occupied destination rules
answers.answer: Draw 1 card first, mandatorily. Then you may move each fighter one at a time up to its move value plus applicable bonuses; each may move zero, and complete one fighter’s movement before starting the next. You may pass through friendly fighters, not opponents, and cannot end in any occupied space.

evidence.text: 1. **Draw 1 card first, mandatory.**

2. **Optionally move** each of your fighters, one at a time, up to your move value (plus applicable bonuses). Each fighter chooses its own distance, including **zero**. Choose their order, but finish one fighter’s movement before starting another’s.

Ordinary movement enters adjacent spaces along connecting lines. You may pass through your own friendly fighters, but **cannot finish in any occupied space**. You may **not pass through opposing fighters**. An effect that moves opposing fighters follows the same rules **from their owner’s perspective**. Apply these movement restrictions to card movement unless that card states an exception.

clauses: BOOST payment and timing/value
Effect of discarded card and allocation of allowance
Defeated fighter card eligibility
answers.answer: During maneuver discard one hand card and add its printed BOOST value to movement; ignore that card’s effects. Each of your fighters receives the boosted allowance. A card unusable because its fighter is defeated may still be discarded to BOOST.

evidence.text: **BOOST movement:** during a maneuver, discard **1 card from your hand** to add its printed **BOOST value** (the small circled number, not its combat value) to the movement value for this maneuver. Each of your fighters receives that allowance. For **any permitted BOOST**, add the discarded card’s BOOST value and **ignore that card’s effects**, whether the BOOST modifies movement or an attack. A card that cannot be played because its fighter is defeated **can still be discarded to BOOST**. Effects may separately permit boosting attacks; boosting is not otherwise a universal option.

clauses: Mandatory draw behavior and empty-deck exhaustion damage per failed draw
No reshuffle and scenario application
answers.answer: Do not reshuffle or decline mandatory draws. With zero cards, both required draws fail separately; each failure deals 2 damage immediately to each of your fighters. Thus your surviving hero and sidekick each take 4 damage (2 + 2).

evidence.text: - Drawing cards, whether from maneuver or an effect, is **mandatory unless explicitly optional**.

- With an empty deck, your fighters are **exhausted**. Each time you must draw a card you cannot draw, **each of your fighters immediately takes 2 damage instead**. Do **not reshuffle** your discard pile. A mandatory draw of 2 with an empty deck therefore causes two separate 2-damage events to every surviving fighter, unless hero defeat has already ended the game. If only one card remains, draw it and take the exhaustion damage for the next missing draw.

clauses: Melee adjacency target rule across zones
Ranged shared-zone rule including disconnected areas
Zone and adjacency definitions
answers.answer: Both melee and ranged fighters may attack an adjacent opponent across zone boundaries. Melee cannot attack a nonadjacent target. Ranged may attack a nonadjacent opponent sharing any zone, including a disconnected part of the same colored zone; the space need not be adjacent. Adjacent and sharing a zone are distinct tests.

evidence.text: 1. **Declare** your attacking fighter (active fighter) and the opposing fighter targeted. Any fighter may attack an **adjacent** opponent, even across zone boundaries. **Melee** fighters may attack only adjacent opponents. **Ranged** fighters may also attack any opponent sharing a zone, regardless of distance or adjacency, including another separated part of that zone.

One fighter per circular space. Spaces connected by a line are **adjacent**. A **zone** consists of all spaces with the same colored pattern, even if separated on the board. A space showing several patterns belongs to all those zones. Adjacency and shared zones are different tests.

clauses: Attack action illegality conditions
Attacker/target declaration and legal cards
Defender option and reveal timing
Versatile card classification for effects
answers.answer: An attack action is illegal without an attack-capable card or a valid target. Declare the attacking fighter and opposing target; the attacker plays a legal attack card, and the defender may decline or play a legal defense card for the defender. Both cards are face down and revealed simultaneously. Versatile cards can attack or defend and count as both attack and defense for other effects; pure defense cannot attack and pure attack cannot defend, and fighter labels apply.

evidence.text: You cannot take an attack action without an attack-capable card in hand or without a valid target for one of your fighters.

1. **Declare** your attacking fighter (active fighter) and the opposing fighter targeted. Any fighter may attack an **adjacent** opponent, even across zone boundaries. **Melee** fighters may attack only adjacent opponents. **Ranged** fighters may also attack any opponent sharing a zone, regardless of distance or adjacency, including another separated part of that zone.

2. **Choose cards:** attacker plays an attack card face down that the attacking fighter is allowed to use. Defender may decline to play a card; otherwise plays a legal defense card face down for the defending fighter. **Reveal simultaneously** after both choices.

Attack-only cards are red, defense-only blue, and **versatile** cards purple. Versatile cards may attack or defend and **count as both attack and defense cards for other effects**. A fighter-specific card cannot be used by a different fighter; **ANY** permits any of your fighters. A pure defense card cannot initiate an attack; a pure attack card cannot defend.

clauses: Combat resolution sequence
Priority for same timing and whether effects are mandatory
Other after-combat effects and final card destinations
answers.answer: Resolve immediately effects, then during-combat effects, then damage/combat result, after-combat card effects, other after-combat game effects, and finally discard played cards to owners’ face-up discard piles. For effects sharing timing, defender resolves first. Effects are mandatory unless they say otherwise.

evidence.text: 1. Resolve **IMMEDIATELY** card effects.

**Whenever effects share a timing, the defender’s effect resolves first.** Card effects are **mandatory unless they say otherwise** (for example “may”); this can harm your own fighters. Complete them in the printed order. A card whose effects are canceled keeps its printed combat value; the canceled effects do not resolve.
6. Finally place all played cards in their respective **face-up discard piles**.

clauses: Equal attack/defense result and subsequent effect damage impact on winner
Damage with no defense card
answers.answer: At 4 versus 4, attack damage is max(4−4,0)=0, so defender wins combat; later 2 effect damage does not change the winner. With no defense card, attack damage is 4.

evidence.text: 3. Determine combat result: defender takes attack value minus defense value, to a minimum of zero. If no defense card, take the attack value. Reduce the defending fighter’s health by the damage dealt. Defense does not itself deal return damage.

**Winning combat is not winning the game:** the attacker wins combat only if the **attack itself** deals at least 1 damage. If it deals none, the **defender wins**, including a tie of values or a defense that prevents the attack damage. Damage from effects does **not** change this winner.

clauses: Sidekick defeat/token and played after-combat effect
Hero defeat immediate game end and pending healing
answers.answer: At zero, remove the defeated sidekick token; its played card still resolves its after-combat effect if the game has not ended. If a hero reaches zero, that hero immediately loses and the game ends; do not resolve pending healing or finish the turn.

evidence.text: There is no points score. Any fighter reduced to **zero health for any reason is defeated**. Immediately remove a defeated sidekick token. A Harpy is defeated by any damage because it has 1 health.
4. Resolve **AFTER COMBAT card effects**. A defeated fighter’s played card still resolves its after-combat effects **unless the game has already ended**.
**A defeated hero immediately loses the duel, and the game ends at once.** Do not continue pending effects to heal that hero or finish the turn. Defeating a sidekick alone does not win the game.
